what_this_is: The explicit allowlist that gates REAL production activation by the release coordinator. ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-006 built the remote validation lane, the trusted artifact handoff, the release queue and a real host adapter, and left this gate EMPTY on purpose. A market is activated for real only when the founder adds it here, names the candidate digest they authorised, and the coordinator's own guards still pass at the moment of the call. There is no implicit opt-in: an empty allowlist means no market can be deployed by this machinery, whatever else is green.
requires_for_each_activation: a founder authorization binding the exact candidate digest, deployment artifact digest, parent release digest and intended delta digest
the live release is still the authorized parent at the moment of the host call
the package receipt (003 rules A-O) and the bundle validation receipt (004) both verify
a CI validation receipt when the change class requires one, or NOT_REQUIRED_BY_POLICY when it does not
the candidate still hashes to its own release manifest
pilot_note: ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-006 produces a RECOMMENDATION for a first pilot market and deploys nothing. The founder chooses the market and authorises the pilot separately.
candidate_binding_note: This gate allowlists a MARKET; it has no candidate-digest allowlist, and the loader (release_coordinator.load_production_gate / production_activation_allowed) reads only RELEASE_COORDINATOR_PRODUCTION_ENABLED and RELEASE_COORDINATOR_PRODUCTION_ALLOWED_MARKETS. The exact-candidate binding is NOT weaker for that: release_coordinator.authorization_problems refuses any candidate whose digest is not the one the authorization binds (CANDIDATE_DIGEST_MISMATCH) and any bundle that is not the authorized artifact (BUNDLE_DIGEST_MISMATCH). The digest above is recorded for audit, not as a control -- writing a field nothing reads and calling it a gate would be worse than having none.

previously_consumed.why_closed: the opening was candidate-specific by design. It authorised ONE market and ONE candidate; that candidate is now live and verified, so the permission has done its job. Closing it restores the empty allowlist, which is what stops a single launch decision from becoming a standing one. The lane itself is untouched: FAST_PATH_IMPLEMENTED and FAST_PATH_VALIDATED stay YES and nothing is disabled.
